intro.title: Reviewing your plan
intro.whatTitle: These are the pages NOVA suggests
intro.whatBody: A plan for the months ahead. Nothing is written or published yet. This is the plan itself, not the content.
intro.extrasTitle: A few extra, as a buffer
intro.extrasBody: Your plan covers a set number of pages a month, and NOVA writes a few more than that as a buffer — extra pages ready to swap in whenever you want to change what's scheduled. Everything past that number waits in the not included tab, at the end of the row of months. Nothing there will be written.
intro.editTitle: Not included, and what Edit does with it
intro.editBody: Open Edit on any month to change it. Take a page out and it moves to not included. Add one from not included and it joins the top of the month you pick. Swap exchanges a page for one in another month, so both months keep the size your plan promises. On a multi-language plan a page and its translations always move together.
intro.extrasMultilocaleTitle: A few extra, as a buffer
intro.extrasMultilocaleBody: Your plan covers a set number of pages a month in each language, and NOVA writes a few more than that as a buffer for when you want to change what's scheduled. Everything past that number waits in the not included tab, at the end of the row of months. Nothing there will be written, and nothing is ever deleted.
intro.editMultilocaleTitle: Changes go through your CSM for now
intro.editMultilocaleBody: Swapping pages yourself isn't available for multi-language plans yet: a swap has to keep every language's monthly count intact, and that part is still being built. Tell your customer service manager which pages you would rather have, and which you would drop, and they will arrange it before the plan is approved.
intro.approveBody: Change what you want, then contact your customer service manager. Approval covers the whole plan in one go, so make your changes first.

reschedule.body: Pick a new publication date. The content is queued to be written again for that date, and the current text is retired straight away — nothing publishes on the new date but the new version.

rewrite.label: Rewrite content
rewrite.title: Rewrite this content
rewrite.body: The page goes back to the writer queue. Whatever has not gone out yet is retired straight away — the client stops seeing it and the page reads as being written again. The new version will need reviewing if review is on for this client.
rewrite.noteDescription: Guidance for the writer — anything it should take into account when it writes this domain's pages.
rewrite.noteLimitHelper: Capped at {max} characters on purpose: the writer works better from short, focused guidance, and a long note crowds out the brief itself.
rewrite.noteScopeTitle: This note belongs to the domain, not to the pages you rewrite
rewrite.noteScopeDescription: Saving a change here rewrites the guidance for every page on this domain that has not been written yet — including ones already queued — and for everything written from now on. Leave it as it is and nothing is saved.
rewrite.noteUnavailableTitle: The content-creation note could not be loaded
rewrite.noteUnavailableDescription: You can still queue the rewrite; the domain's saved note is left exactly as it is. Reopen this dialog later to edit it.
rewrite.inYourCmsTitle: The draft in the client's CMS stays
rewrite.inYourCmsDescription: This page has already been handed to the client's CMS, and NOVA cannot take a draft back once it is theirs. The rewrite puts a new version beside it rather than replacing it, so ask them to discard the old draft.
rewrite.lapsedDescription: Reschedule the post instead — that moves the date and re-queues the write in one step. A publication date in the past is skipped, so a rewrite on its own would never go out.

editUrl.label: Edit URL manually
editUrl.title: Edit this page's URL
editUrl.body: Set the path this page will be published at. The plan's slug is updated to match, so the address on screen and the one the pipeline builds cannot disagree.
editUrl.publishedBody: Correct the path to match where the page actually is. The plan's slug is updated to match, so the address on screen and the one the pipeline builds cannot disagree.
editUrl.publishedDescription: Saving corrects what NOVA has on file. It does not move the page that is already live — move that in the client's CMS first, then record the new address here. Anything still queued for this page publishes at the address recorded here. Search Console reports a page under the address it was crawled at, so this page's clicks and impressions restart from whatever Google has for the new one.
